title: Project Rotation Fellowship (RPF) — Launch & Operations Manual

Overview

This document describes the Project Rotation Fellowship (RPF), an opt-in program that supports cross-team skills development, rapid onboarding into adjacent domains, and internal mobility at Redwood. The RPF is a 6–12 week, project-oriented rotation designed for ICs and early managers who want hands-on experience in a different product area, platform team, or customer success track while keeping their core role and compensation intact.

Purpose and goals

- Accelerate skill acquisition for high-impact, cross-functional projects.
- Reduce time-to-contribution when employees move to new teams or take on hybrid responsibilities.
- Improve internal mobility rates and reduce hiring ramp costs.
- Create repeatable handoff artifacts and templates that preserve institutional knowledge.

Program variants

- Short Fellowship (6 weeks): Focused learning sprint with one well-scoped deliverable. Best for tooling, docs, or experiment-driven work.
- Standard Fellowship (9 weeks): Balanced discovery + delivery rhythm; includes a small end-to-end feature or migration task.
- Deep Fellowship (12 weeks): For complex integrations, security/compliance projects, or multi-team migration planning.

Eligibility and nomination

- Who can apply: Regular ICs (L2–L5), staff-level engineers with manager consent, product managers, and member-of-staff customer success leads.
- Manager approval: A written manager sign-off is required and must include a statement of support and a continuity plan for the fellow's home responsibilities.
- Skill fit: Fellowship proposals must map to at least two measurable learning objectives and one deliverable for the host team.
- Frequency: An individual may participate in the RPF up to twice in any 24-month period; exceptions require director-level approval.

Key roles and responsibilities

- Fellow (participant)
  - Own learning objectives, attend host team ceremonies, and deliver the agreed project artifact.
  - Maintain weekly updates to the home manager and host lead.
- Home manager
  - Provide approval, maintain backfill plan (short-term coverage or task reprioritization), and maintain performance context.
- Host lead
  - Assign a mentor, define the scope, and ensure access to systems and documentation.
- Mentor (primary contact on the host team)
  - Provide day-to-day guidance, onboarding to codebase and tooling, and review deliverables.
- People Ops (program owner)
  - Coordinate nominations, maintain fellowship schedule, run kickoff and wrap ceremonies, and keep program metrics.

Selection process and timeline

1. Proposal submission (Week -3 to -2): Fellow or manager submits a 1-page proposal: goals, proposed host team, duration, and success criteria.
2. Triage (Week -2): People Ops validates eligibility and confirms host team capacity.
3. Approvals (Week -2 to -1): Home manager and host lead sign the rotation agreement.
4. Kickoff (Day 0): Program kickoff with People Ops, host mentor, fellow, and home manager. Agree on communication cadence, tooling access, and handoff milestones.
5. Midpoint check-in (Week 3–6): Formal review between the fellow, mentor, and home manager to adjust scope if needed.
6. Wrap & knowledge transfer (Final week): Document handoff, close tickets, and present outcomes at a cross-team demo.

Rotation agreement template (1-page)

- Title: [Fellow name] — [Host team] — [Duration]
- Learning objectives: • Objective 1 • Objective 2
- Deliverable(s): • Artifact A (link) • Artifact B (link)
- Duration and schedule: [start date] — [end date], expected weekly hours committed to host
- Success criteria: 3 measurable acceptance checks
- Approvals: Home manager | Host lead | People Ops

Access and tooling checklist (example table)

| Category | Items | Responsible | Target complete |
|---------|-------|-------------|----------------|
| Codebase | Repo access (read/write), CI runner tokens | Host lead | Day 2 |
| Jira | Project write access, issue templates | Host lead | Day 2 |
| Slack | Host team channel + #rpf-fellows | People Ops | Day 1 |
| Cloud / Infra | Role-based access, test environment | Host lead + Security | Day 3 |
| Analytics | Dashboard viewers, query access | Host lead | Day 4 |

Onboarding & first-week cadence

- Day 0: Kickoff meeting, rotation agreement sign-off, access checklist start.
- Day 1–2: Codebase walkthrough, repo onboarding, run a local dev build, join host team standup and planning.
- Day 3–5: Shadow mentor on core workflows, pick up first small task, weekly 1:1 scheduled with home manager and mentor.

Performance management and compensation

- The fellow remains on their home manager's org and payroll; there is no compensation change for standard rotations.
- Performance feedback for the rotation is fed into the fellow's regular performance cycle by the home manager; the host lead provides a written rotation evaluation for the fellow's file.
- Promotions and role changes resulting from the rotation are handled through standard promotion/transfer processes and require manager/director approval.

Reporting, success metrics, and program KPIs

People Ops will track and publish the following quarterly:
- Fellowship count and completion rate (target completion >= 90%).
- Average time to first meaningful contribution on host team (target <= 3 weeks for 6–9 week rotations).
- Internal mobility conversion: percent of fellows who transfer roles within 12 months (target 18%+).
- Fellow satisfaction (post-fellow NPS; target >= 8/10).
- Document artifact quality: percent of handoffs with complete docs and runbooks (target >= 95%).

Knowledge capture and handoff requirements

- Every fellowship must close with a Confluence handoff page located under: /confluence/teams/[host-team]/rpf-handoffs/[fellow-name]-YYYYMMDD.
- Required artifacts:
  - Architecture decision notes or design doc
  - Runbooks for anything operated in production
  - Test plan and known failure modes
  - A clear list of tickets left open and who will own them post-rotation

Budgeting and perks

- People Ops maintains a small rotation budget for cross-team learning. Typical reimbursable items include conference passes (pre-approved), short dedicated training, and workspace ergonomics for a remote fellow.
- Fellows are eligible for a one-time learning stipend (up to $800) to cover books, courses, or small equipment purchases, pending manager sign-off.
- Hosts can request a temporary headcount shadow (up to 2 weeks) for critical backfill; approvals routed through People Ops.

Risk management and security

- Sensitive projects (PII, audited) require a security review prior to approval. Host lead must list data accesses and sign off with Security.
- If a rotation overlaps scheduled on-call windows, explicit contingency coverage must be documented before Day 0.
- Hosts are responsible for ensuring fellows follow the host team's incident escalation and access policies.

Wrap ceremony and knowledge sharing

- All completed fellowships are celebrated in the RPF wrap ceremony (monthly hybrid town hall) where fellows present a 10-minute demo and learning recap.
- Post-fellow writeups are published to a shared RPF Confluence space and linked to the home manager's performance notes.

Measurement and continuous improvement

- People Ops will run bi-annual retrospectives with host leads and a representative set of fellows to iterate on the program.
- The RPF handbook will be updated annually or following significant process changes.

FAQs

- Q: Can fellows be on partial rotations (e.g., 50% time)?
  - A: Yes, with explicit manager and host lead approval; these are considered "embedded rotations" and require a more detailed continuity plan.
- Q: Does the fellow keep their equity vesting schedule? 
  - A: Yes, compensation and equity schedules are unchanged.
- Q: Who owns the final deliverable?
  - A: The host team owns the deliverable post-handoff unless otherwise negotiated in the rotation agreement.

Related links and templates

- Rotation agreement template: /confluence/templates/rpf-agreement
- Confluence handoff template: /confluence/templates/rpf-handoff
- People Ops program calendar: /confluence/people-ops/rpf-schedule

Stakeholders and escalation

- Program owner: People Ops (Primary contact: people-ops@redwood.ai)
- Escalations: Home manager -> Host lead -> Director of People Ops
- Security review: Security (security@redwood.ai) for regulated projects

Revision history

- 2028-02-15: Version 1.0 — initial published manual (People Ops author)
- 2028-03-01: Version 1.1 — clarified embedded rotation policy and added stipend details
